dailyInsight.headline: Audit whether an agent can rewrite the instructions that will steer its next session
dailyInsight.insight: Hermes Agent's fresh protected-instruction write gate supports one bounded audit for people operating coding agents in shared repositories: inventory the project files that can become later agent instructions, then check whether changing each one requires a fresh human decision rather than inheriting an earlier broad approval. The inspected source distinguishes those high-leverage persistence targets from ordinary working files and refuses the protected write when no human approval channel exists.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The public implementation matches normalized and real paths for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, SOUL.md, .cursorrules, and immediate project-local .hermes configuration. It uses a separate one-operation approval path rather than the ordinary yolo or session-persistent gate, treats one protected target as a stop for a whole multi-file patch, and includes focused tests for traversal, symlinks, repeated writes, and no-human failure.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A permission that is reasonable for editing application code can be too broad for changing material that a later agent session treats as instruction. Separating an ordinary file edit from a persistence-changing edit gives operators a concrete review point before one task silently changes the next task's starting conditions.

actions.audience: Builder or operator who lets coding agents edit shared repositories
actions.label: Trace one instruction-file write path
actions.instruction: In a disposable clone with no production credentials, list every project-controlled file your coding agent can load as instructions, settings, skills, or prompt context. Attempt a harmless edit to one such file and verify that the exact write path requires fresh, one-time human approval even when ordinary edits are auto-approved. Test a symlink or normalized-path variant only in the disposable clone; do not use the drill to modify a live policy file.

receipts.title: Protected agent-instruction files always require write approval
receipts.supports: Shows the fresh source change, protected file set, separate one-operation approval rule, no-human failure behavior, configuration defaults, and focused test coverage.

confidence.basis: The fresh public commit, directly inspected file-tool implementation, configuration default, and focused file-write tests agree on the narrow protected-instruction boundary and its yolo-resistant approval behavior.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are public source and test receipts from Hermes Agent main. They do not establish a released version, independent security testing, coverage of every terminal or tool write route, all instruction loaders, or prevention of every prompt-injection vector.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if a public regression shows that a protected project instruction file can be rewritten through the covered write or patch paths without a fresh prompt, if an inherited auto-approval bypasses the separate gate, or if the documented scope excludes a named file the tool loads as project instruction.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for public end-to-end adversarial tests that carry a protected write attempt through later instruction loading, terminal execution, and another agent session; those tests will show how far the narrow file-tool boundary reaches.
